title: Dependency Resilience Playbook and Ownership Roulette
creator: Leah Ortiz
description:
Problem: Cross-team dependencies (Eng, Design, Security, Infra) regularly create last-mile churn during quarter cutovers. We lack a lightweight, repeatable playbook and tooling to surface dependency risk early, assign temporary risk owners automatically, and enforce SLA-backed gating for roadmap commits.

Goal: Create a dependency resilience playbook + a small automated service ("Ownership Roulette") that: 1) computes a dependency resilience score from multiple signals, 2) increments a countdown to checkpoint dates, 3) rotates a short-term risk owner when a dependency is stale, and 4) auto-triggers escalation workflows and gating flags on the roadmap if thresholds are hit.

Scope: Product + Engineering + Design + Security + Infra. Work includes product spec, priority scoring formula, lightweight ownership rotation rules, dashboard telemetry in Redwood Console, Linear/Slack integration for alerts, and docs/playbook. This is not a replacement for long-term ownership—it's a temporary risk mitigation mechanism and timeline enforcement tool to reduce late-stage surprises for release windows.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Resilience score is computable for any tracked dependency using: issue status (Linear), ETA confidence (PM input), linked PRs, owner capacity (oncall/roster), and mitigation plan presence.
A2: Console dashboard panel created showing per-initiative dependency list, resilience score, days-to-checkpoint, and current risk owner; supports filtering by team and release window.

A3: Ownership Roulette service created: when a dependency is 'stale' for > X days before checkpoint, it assigns a temporary risk owner from a configurable pool and posts a notification to the dependency's Slack channel and Linear thread.
A4: Automatic escalation path implemented: if resilience score <= threshold Y within 7 days of checkpoint, auto-open an escalation ticket assigned to initiative lead and notify SLT channel.
A5: Playbook doc published (Confluence) with step-by-step runbook, roles, SLAs, and rollback guidance, and at least two initiative teams trial the flow during the next cutover window.

A6: Metrics instrumented: mean time to resolution after rotation, false-positive rate of ownership assignment, and number of blocked cutovers reduced by > 25% in trial teams (measured in next release window).
notes: Trade-offs: automated rotation eases bottlenecks but risks temporary owner friction—opt-in default for non-production critical initiatives recommended.
Data sources: Linear issue metadata, linked GitHub PR status, Console model of release windows, team oncall/roster (HR sync), and PM-provided ETA confidence field.

Implementation approach: Start with a rules engine in roadmap service that computes score; expose scoring endpoint; build a Console panel and a small lambda for Slack/Linear automation. Phase 1 will be read-only scoring + dashboard; Phase 2 enables rotations and escalations.

Operational concerns: ensure rota assignments respect ownership blacklist (eg. security leads should not be rotatable); include audit log for all auto-assignments; allow manual override from initiative lead.

Open question: acceptable default thresholds for 'stale' and 'low resilience'—propose: stale = 10 business days before checkpoint with no progress; low resilience score <= 0.35 (normalized). Need cross-team alignment during kickoff.
Localization: Slack channels vary by org — map by team alias; fallback to PM DMs when channel absent.
Success criteria for pilot: two initiatives in Q2 adopt playbook and show measurable reduction in last-week blockers; teams opt-in for rotation pool after pilot feedback.
